newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly quiet Tuesday morning trade, dealers said.
The market opened in surplus of Z$500 million and the Reserve Bank offered Z$500 million worth of 30-day treasury bills to discount houses.

The previous day, the central bank held two treasury bill auctions for 66-day treasury bills. The first raised Z$440 million at 22.94 percent while the second raised Z$280 million with an average yield of 22.99 percent.

Dealers said there was not much activity on the secondary market on Tuesday with most rates being merely indicative. Treasury bills were being sold on the market at 22.25 percent and call money was at 20 percent from 22.5 percent.
NCD bills with 30-, 60- and 90-day maturities were quoted at 25 and 22 percent (buying and selling respectively) while Bankers acceptances were being bought at 23.5 percent and sold at 22.25 percent.
